turns.response_html:
The SBA's business planning guide outlines several critical stages for turning an idea into a functional small business. Each step is designed to help you understand your market, structure your operations, and secure the necessary capital.

1. Market Research and Competitive Analysis

This stage involves gathering data to determine if there is a real opportunity for your business.

  • Market Research: Helps you identify potential customers, their buying habits, and the demand for your product or service.
  • Competitive Analysis: Focuses on finding your "edge" by studying what other businesses in your niche are doing well and where they are failing.

2. Write Your Business Plan

A business plan serves as the foundation and roadmap for your company. It is often required if you are seeking outside investment or loans. The SBA typically highlights two common formats:

  • Traditional Business Plan: Very detailed, comprehensive, and used when seeking significant funding.
  • Lean Startup Plan: High-level and focuses on the most important elements of your business model.

3. Calculate Startup Costs

Before launching, you need a clear picture of your initial expenses. This includes:

  • One-time costs: Such as incorporation fees, equipment, and initial signage.
  • Ongoing costs: Such as rent, utilities, and insurance for the first few months. Knowing these numbers helps you estimate when you will reach "break-even" and start turning a profit.

4. Establish Business Credit

Developing a credit history for your business is distinct from your personal credit. This step involves:

  • Applying for a federal tax ID (EIN).
  • Opening a business bank account.
  • Maintaining a positive payment history with vendors to build a score that allows for better loan terms later.

5. Fund Your Business

How you choose to fund your business can impact its legal structure and daily operations. Common sources include:

  • Self-funding: Using your own savings.
  • Investors: Pitching to venture capitalists or angel investors.
  • Loans: Applying for SBA-guaranteed loans or traditional commercial bank loans.

6. Consider Buying an Existing Business or Franchise

As an alternative to starting from scratch, the SBA provides guidance on purchasing a business that is already operational. This can simplify the planning process as the market research and infrastructure are often already in place.

turns.prompt_text: How do I set a reminder in Google Keep when I enter a specific location?
turns.response_html:
To set a location-based reminder in Google Keep, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Note: Select the note you want to add a reminder to or create a new one.
  2. Access Reminders: Tap the Bell icon (Remind me) usually found at the top right of the note.
  3. Choose Location: Select Place (or "Pick a place").
  4. Enter Address: Type in the name or the specific address of the location. Google Keep will offer suggestions as you type.
  5. Save: Once the location is selected, tap Save.

Essential Troubleshooting for Location Reminders

For these reminders to trigger correctly when you arrive, ensure the following settings are enabled on your device:

  • Location Permissions: Google Keep must have "Always" or "While using the app" access to your location.
  • Precision: Ensure "Use precise location" is toggled on in your device's app settings for Keep.
  • Battery Optimization: On some devices, "Battery Saver" modes can prevent the app from checking your location in the background. Ensure Keep is not being restricted by power-saving settings.
  • Internet Connection: You generally need a data connection or Wi-Fi for the device to verify your coordinates against the saved address.

turns.prompt_text: I do not see that option. I see a menu that says "Pick a date and time".
turns.response_html:
If you only see "Pick a date and time," it usually means the app does not have the necessary permissions to access your location. To reveal the "Pick a place" option, you typically need to enable location services for Google Keep in your device settings.

How to enable the location option:

  1. Open Device Settings: Go to your phone's main Settings app.
  2. Find App Permissions: Tap on Apps (or Apps & notifications) and select Keep Notes.
  3. Enable Location: Tap on Permissions, then Location.
  4. Set to Always or While Using: Change the setting to "Allow only while using the app" or "Ask every time." * Note: For the reminder to actually trigger while the app is closed, you may eventually need to select "Allow all the time" if your version of Android/iOS supports it.
  5. Restart Keep: Close the Google Keep app completely and reopen it.

Once permissions are granted, when you tap the bell icon, you should see two distinct tabs or options: Time and Place.

Additional Check

If permissions are already on and you still don't see it, ensure Location (GPS) is turned on in your phone's quick settings (the pull-down menu). On some versions of the app, the "Place" option is a separate tab at the top of the reminder menu.
